requirements.original: The alive operation is a Boolean operation that checks whether a test component has been created and is ready to execute or is executing already a behaviour.
requirements.canonical: The `alive` operation IS a Boolean operation that checks whether a test component has been created and is ready to execute or is already executing a behaviour.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- The alive operation is a Boolean operation that checks whether a test component has been created and is ready to execute or is executing already a behaviour.

requirements.original: ( ObjectReference | any component | all component | any from ComponentArrayRef ) "." alive [ "->" @index value ValueRef ]
requirements.canonical: The `alive` operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | `any component` | `all component` | `any from` ComponentArrayRef ) "." `alive` [ "->" `@index` `value` ValueRef ].

examples.text:
pTC1.done;  // Waits for termination of the component
  if (pTC1.alive) { // If the component is still alive …
     pTC1.start(f_anotherFunction()); // … execute another function on it.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- ( ObjectReference | any component | all component | any from ComponentArrayRef ) "." alive [ "->" @index value ValueRef ]

requirements.original: Applied on a normal parallel test component, the alive operation returns true if the component is inactive or running a behaviour and false otherwise.
requirements.canonical: Applied on a non-alive PTC, the `alive` operation IS true if the component is inactive or running a behaviour.

ambiguity.issue: 'normal parallel test component' is used for a non-alive PTC.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- Applied on a normal parallel test component, the alive operation returns true if the component is inactive or running a behaviour and false otherwise.

requirements.original: Applied on a normal parallel test component, the alive operation returns true if the component is inactive or running a behaviour and false otherwise.
requirements.canonical: Applied on a non-alive PTC that is neither inactive nor running a behaviour, the `alive` operation IS false.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- Applied on a normal parallel test component, the alive operation returns true if the component is inactive or running a behaviour and false otherwise.

requirements.original: Applied on an alive-type parallel component, the operation returns true if the component is inactive, running or stopped.
requirements.canonical: Applied on an alive-type PTC, the `alive` operation IS true if the component is inactive, running or stopped.

examples.text:
pTC1.done;  // Waits for termination of the component
  if (pTC1.alive) { // If the component is still alive …
     pTC1.start(f_anotherFunction()); // … execute another function on it.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- Applied on an alive-type parallel component, the operation returns true if the component is inactive, running or stopped.

requirements.original: It returns false if the component has been killed.
requirements.canonical: Applied on an alive-type PTC that has been killed, the `alive` operation IS false.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- It returns false if the component has been killed.

requirements.original: Applied on the mtc the operation returns true.
requirements.canonical: Applied on the MTC, the `alive` operation IS true.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- Applied on the mtc the operation returns true.

requirements.original: In particular, in combination with the all keyword it returns true if all (alive-type or normal) PTCs are alive.
requirements.canonical: The `all component.alive` operation IS true if all PTCs (alive-type or non-alive) are alive.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- In particular, in combination with the all keyword it returns true if all (alive-type or normal) PTCs are alive.

requirements.original: The alive operation used in combination with the any keyword returns true if at least one PTC is alive.
requirements.canonical: The `any component.alive` operation IS true if at least one PTC is alive.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- The alive operation used in combination with the any keyword returns true if at least one PTC is alive.

requirements.original: When the any from component array notation is used, the components from the referenced array are iterated over and individually checked for being inactive or running a function from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.
requirements.canonical: When the `any from` component array notation is used with the `alive` operation, each component of the referenced array IS checked in turn, iterating from innermost to outermost dimension and from lowest to highest index for each dimension.

ambiguity.issue: The components are said to be checked for 'being inactive or running a function', which conflicts with 21.3.5-s004 (a stopped alive-type component is also alive) and ignores altstep behaviours. The reading consistent with the alive semantics of single components is chosen.
readings: With `any from`, each component of the array IS checked for being alive as defined for a single component (for alive-type PTCs, inactive, running or stopped), iterating from innermost to outermost dimension and from lowest to highest index.
With `any from`, each component of the array IS checked only for being inactive or running a function, iterating from innermost to outermost dimension and from lowest to highest index.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- When the any from component array notation is used, the components from the referenced array are iterated over and individually checked for being inactive or running a function from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.

requirements.original: The first component to be found being inactive or running a behaviour causes the alive operation to return the true value.
requirements.canonical: When the `any from` component array notation is used, the `alive` operation IS true as soon as the first component found inactive or running a behaviour is reached.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- The first component to be found being inactive or running a behaviour causes the alive operation to return the true value.

requirements.original: The index of the first component found alive can optionally be assigned to an integer variable for single-dimensional component arrays or to an integer array or record of integer variable for multi-dimensional component arrays.
requirements.canonical: The index of the first component found alive MAY be assigned to an integer variable for a single-dimensional component array, or to an integer array or record of integer variable for a multi-dimensional component array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- The index of the first component found alive can optionally be assigned to an integer variable for single-dimensional component arrays or to an integer array or record of integer variable for multi-dimensional component arrays.

requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of an `alive` operation SHALL be of component type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of an `alive` operation SHALL NOT resolve to a template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.original: b) The ComponentArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized component array.
requirements.canonical: The ComponentArrayRef of an `alive` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized component array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- b) The ComponentArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized component array.

requirements.original: c) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from component array construct.
requirements.canonical: The index redirection of an `alive` operation SHALL only be used when the operation is applied on an `any from` component array construct.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- c) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from component array construct.

requirements.original: d) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional component arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective array.
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional component array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the array.
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional component array
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- d) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional component arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective array.

requirements.original: e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional component array, the size of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL be exactly the same as the dimension of the array.
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional component array
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.original: e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional component array, the element type of the integer array or record of integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional component array
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.original: f) If a variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the alive operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the alive operation.
requirements.canonical: If a variable referenced in the `@index` clause of an `alive` operation is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the index value assigned to it IS the value produced by the `alive` operation; a later evaluation of the variable does not invoke the `alive` operation again.
requirements.condition: the variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable

ambiguity.issue: The text says 'the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the alive operation', but the @index clause receives the index of the found component, not the Boolean result. The reading that the stored index value is meant is chosen.
readings: A lazy or fuzzy variable referenced in the `@index` clause IS assigned the index value determined by the `alive` operation, and later evaluation of it does not invoke the `alive` operation again.
A lazy or fuzzy variable referenced in the `@index` clause IS assigned the Boolean result of the `alive` operation, and later evaluation of it does not invoke the `alive` operation again.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.5 -- f) If a variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the alive operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the alive operation.

requirements.original: ( ObjectReference | any component | all component | any from ComponentArrayRef ) "." running [ "->" @index value ValueRef]
requirements.canonical: The `running` operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | `any component` | `all component` | `any from` ComponentArrayRef ) "." `running` [ "->" `@index` `value` ValueRef ].
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- ( ObjectReference | any component | all component | any from ComponentArrayRef ) "." running [ "->" @index value ValueRef]

requirements.original: The running operation allows behaviour executing on a test component to ascertain whether behaviour running on a different component has completed.
requirements.canonical: The `running` operation CAN be used by behaviour executing on a test component to ascertain whether behaviour running on a different test component has completed.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- The running operation allows behaviour executing on a test component to ascertain whether behaviour running on a different component has completed.

requirements.original: The running operation returns true for the mtc and PTCs that have been started but not yet terminated or stopped.
requirements.canonical: The `running` operation returns `true` for the MTC and for a PTC that has been started but not yet terminated or stopped.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- The running operation returns true for the mtc and PTCs that have been started but not yet terminated or stopped.

requirements.original: It returns false otherwise.
requirements.canonical: The `running` operation returns `false` for a test component that has not been started or has already terminated or been stopped.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- It returns false otherwise.

requirements.original: The running operation is considered to be a boolean expression and, thus, returns a boolean value to indicate whether the specified test component (or all test components) has terminated.
requirements.canonical: The `running` operation IS a boolean expression that returns a boolean value indicating whether the specified test component (or all test components) is still executing.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence says the result indicates whether the component "has terminated", which contradicts s004/s005 where true means still executing; the reading consistent with s004 was chosen.
readings: The `running` operation returns `true` if the specified test component is still executing.
The `running` operation returns a value indicating whether the specified test component has terminated (true meaning terminated).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- The running operation is considered to be a boolean expression and, thus, returns a boolean value to indicate whether the specified test component (or all test components) has terminated.

requirements.original: In contrast to the done operation, the running operation can be used freely in boolean expressions.
requirements.canonical: In contrast to the `done` operation, the `running` operation MAY be used freely in boolean expressions.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- In contrast to the done operation, the running operation can be used freely in boolean expressions.

requirements.original: When the all keyword is used with the running operation, it will return true if all PTCs started but not stopped explicitly by another component are executing their behaviour.
requirements.canonical: `all component.running` returns `true` if all PTCs that have been started but not stopped explicitly by another component are executing their behaviour.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether PTCs that terminated on their own (not stopped explicitly by another component) are excluded or make the result false.
readings: `all component.running` returns `true` if every started PTC, except those stopped explicitly by another component, is still executing.
`all component.running` returns `true` only if every started PTC is still executing, regardless of how it stopped.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- When the all keyword is used with the running operation, it will return true if all PTCs started but not stopped explicitly by another component are executing their behaviour.

requirements.original: Otherwise it returns false.
requirements.canonical: `all component.running` returns `false` if not all PTCs started but not stopped explicitly by another component are executing their behaviour.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- Otherwise it returns false.

requirements.original: NOTE: The difference between the running operation applied to a single ptc and the usage of the all keyword leads to the situation that ptc.running is false if the ptc has never been started but all component.running is true at the same time as it considers only those components that ever have been started.
requirements.canonical: `ptc.running` IS `false` for a PTC that has never been started, while `all component.running` can be `true` at the same time because it considers only PTCs that have been started.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- NOTE: The difference between the running operation applied to a single ptc and the usage of the all keyword leads to the situation that ptc.running is false if the ptc has never been started but all component.running is true at the same time as it considers only those components that ever have been started.

requirements.original: When the any keyword is used with the running operation, it will return true if at least one PTC is executing its behaviour.
requirements.canonical: `any component.running` returns `true` if at least one PTC is executing its behaviour.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- When the any keyword is used with the running operation, it will return true if at least one PTC is executing its behaviour.

requirements.original: Otherwise it returns false.
requirements.canonical: `any component.running` returns `false` if no PTC is executing its behaviour.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- Otherwise it returns false.

requirements.original: When the any from component array notation is used, the components from the referenced array are iterated over and individually checked for executing currently from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.
requirements.canonical: When the `any from` component array notation is used with the `running` operation, each component of the referenced array IS checked individually for executing, iterating from innermost to outermost dimension and from lowest to highest index within each dimension.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- When the any from component array notation is used, the components from the referenced array are iterated over and individually checked for executing currently from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.

requirements.original: The first component to be found executing causes the running operation to succeed.
requirements.canonical: With the `any from` component array notation, the first component found executing causes the `running` operation to succeed.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- The first component to be found executing causes the running operation to succeed.

requirements.original: The index of the matched component can optionally be assigned to an integer variable for single-dimensional arrays or to an integer array or record of integer variable for multi-dimensional component arrays.
requirements.canonical: The index of the component matched by the `running` operation with `any from` MAY be assigned to an integer variable for a single-dimensional component array, or to an integer array or record of integer variable for a multi-dimensional component array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- The index of the matched component can optionally be assigned to an integer variable for single-dimensional arrays or to an integer array or record of integer variable for multi-dimensional component arrays.

requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of the `running` operation SHALL be of a component type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of the `running` operation SHALL NOT resolve to a template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.original: b) The ComponentArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized component array.
requirements.canonical: The ComponentArrayRef of the `running` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized component array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- b) The ComponentArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized component array.

requirements.original: c) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from component array construct.
requirements.canonical: The index redirection of the `running` operation SHALL only be used when the operation is applied to an `any from` component array construct.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- c) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from component array construct.

requirements.original: d) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional component arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective array.
requirements.canonical: The type of the integer variable used in the index redirection SHALL allow storing the highest index of the single-dimensional component array.
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional component array
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- d) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional component arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective array.

requirements.original: e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.
requirements.canonical: The size of the integer array or record of integer type used in the index redirection SHALL be exactly the same as the number of dimensions of the multi-dimensional component array.
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional component array

ambiguity.issue: "size ... the same as the dimension" could mean the number of dimensions or the size of a dimension.
readings: The size of the integer array or record of integer SHALL equal the number of dimensions of the component array.
The size of the integer array or record of integer SHALL equal the size of a dimension of the component array.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.original: e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.
requirements.canonical: The element type of the integer array or record of integer used in the index redirection SHALL allow storing the highest index of all dimensions of the multi-dimensional component array.
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional component array
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.original: f) If a variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the running operation.
requirements.canonical: If a variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to that variable IS equal to the result produced by the `running` operation.
requirements.condition: the variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- f) If a variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the running operation.

requirements.original: Later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the running operation.
requirements.canonical: Later evaluation of a lazy or fuzzy variable referenced in the @index clause IS NOT a repeated invocation of the `running` operation.
requirements.condition: the variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.header: // @requirement: 21.3.6 -- Later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the running operation.
